nonprofit-990:totrevenue: Total revenue for the year is a financial measure that counts all income generated by a nonprofit organization during its fiscal year. This figure encompasses various sources of revenue, including contributions, grants, and program service income. It is distinct from total functional expenses, as it focuses solely on income rather than expenditures. The unit of measurement is in dollars, reported per organization per fiscal year.
nonprofit-990:totfuncexpns: Total expenses for the year represents the overall financial outlay of a nonprofit organization during its fiscal year. This measure includes all functional expenses incurred, such as program services, administrative costs, and fundraising expenses. It is different from total revenue, as it focuses on the costs rather than the income generated. The unit of measurement is in dollars, reported per organization per fiscal year.
nonprofit-990:totassetsend: Total assets at the end of the year reflects the complete value of all resources owned by a nonprofit organization as of the end of its fiscal year. This measure includes cash, investments, property, and other assets, providing a snapshot of the organization's financial health. It is distinct from total liabilities, which accounts for the organization's obligations, and focuses solely on what the organization owns. The unit of measurement is in dollars, reported per organization per fiscal year.
nonprofit-990:totliabend: Total liabilities at the end of the year indicates the total amount of financial obligations that a nonprofit organization has as of the end of its fiscal year. This measure includes debts, loans, and other liabilities, providing insight into the organization's financial responsibilities. It is different from total assets, which measures what the organization owns, and focuses exclusively on what it owes. The unit of measurement is in dollars, reported per organization per fiscal year.
nonprofit-990:totnetassetend: Net assets or fund balances at the end of the year represent the difference between total assets and total liabilities for a nonprofit organization as of the end of its fiscal year. This measure indicates the organization's financial position and sustainability, showing how much is left after all obligations are met. It is distinct from total assets and total liabilities, as it provides a net figure rather than gross amounts. The unit of measurement is in dollars, reported per organization per fiscal year.
nonprofit-990:totcntrbgfts: Contributions, gifts, and grants received is a financial measure that counts all forms of donations and financial support a nonprofit organization has received during its fiscal year. This figure includes individual donations, corporate gifts, and grants from foundations or government entities. It is different from total revenue, as it specifically focuses on voluntary contributions rather than all income sources. The unit of measurement is in dollars, reported per organization per fiscal year.
nonprofit-990:totprgmrevnue: Total program service revenue reflects the income generated from the primary activities and services provided by a nonprofit organization during its fiscal year. This measure includes fees for services, sales of goods related to the mission, and other income directly tied to program activities. It is distinct from total revenue, as it focuses solely on income derived from program services rather than all sources of income. The unit of measurement is in dollars, reported per organization per fiscal year.
nonprofit-990:invstmntinc: Investment income is a financial measure that counts the earnings generated from the nonprofit organization's investments during its fiscal year. This figure includes interest, dividends, and capital gains from various investment vehicles. It is different from total revenue, as it specifically pertains to income derived from investments rather than operational activities or contributions. The unit of measurement is in dollars, reported per organization per fiscal year.
nonprofit-990:compnsatncurrofcr: Compensation of current officers, directors, trustees, and key employees is a financial measure that reports the total salary and benefits paid to the leadership of a nonprofit organization during its fiscal year. This figure includes all forms of compensation, such as wages, bonuses, and other benefits. It is distinct from salaries and wages paid to other employees, as it specifically focuses on the organization's top leadership. The unit of measurement is in dollars, reported per organization per fiscal year.
nonprofit-990:othrsalwages: Other salaries and wages paid to employees is a financial measure that counts the total compensation provided to all employees of a nonprofit organization, excluding current officers and key personnel, during its fiscal year. This figure includes regular salaries, wages, and any additional compensation for staff. It is different from officer compensation, as it encompasses all non-leadership employees. The unit of measurement is in dollars, reported per organization per fiscal year.
nonprofit-990:payrolltx: Payroll taxes paid is a financial measure that reports the total amount of taxes a nonprofit organization has paid on behalf of its employees during its fiscal year. This figure includes federal, state, and local payroll taxes, which are mandatory contributions based on employee wages. It is distinct from salaries and wages, as it specifically pertains to tax obligations rather than direct compensation. The unit of measurement is in dollars, reported per organization per fiscal year.
nonprofit-990:profndraising: Professional fundraising fees represent the total amount paid by a nonprofit organization for services rendered by external fundraising professionals during its fiscal year. This measure includes fees for consulting, event planning, and other fundraising-related services. It is different from direct fundraising expenses, as it focuses specifically on payments to professional fundraisers rather than the costs associated with fundraising events. The unit of measurement is in dollars, reported per organization per fiscal year.
nonprofit-990:grsincfndrsng: Gross income from fundraising events is a financial measure that counts the total revenue generated from all fundraising activities conducted by a nonprofit organization during its fiscal year. This figure includes ticket sales, donations received during events, and other income directly related to fundraising efforts. It is distinct from net fundraising income, as it does not account for any expenses incurred during these events. The unit of measurement is in dollars, reported per organization per fiscal year.
nonprofit-990:lessdirfndrsng: Direct expenses of fundraising events represent the total costs incurred by a nonprofit organization in conducting its fundraising activities during its fiscal year. This measure includes expenses such as venue rental, catering, and promotional materials directly related to fundraising events. It is different from gross income from fundraising events, as it focuses solely on the costs rather than the revenue generated. The unit of measurement is in dollars, reported per organization per fiscal year.
nonprofit-990:netincfndrsng: Net income or loss from fundraising events is a financial measure that calculates the difference between gross income from fundraising events and direct fundraising expenses for a nonprofit organization during its fiscal year. This figure indicates the overall profitability of fundraising activities. It is distinct from gross income, as it accounts for expenses, providing a clearer picture of financial performance. The unit of measurement is in dollars, reported per organization per fiscal year.
nonprofit-990:grsincgaming: Gross income from gaming is a financial measure that counts the total revenue generated from gaming activities conducted by a nonprofit organization during its fiscal year. This figure includes all income from gaming events, such as bingo, raffles, and casino nights. It is different from net gaming income, as it does not account for any expenses related to these gaming activities. The unit of measurement is in dollars, reported per organization per fiscal year.
nonprofit-990:lessdirgaming: Direct expenses of gaming represent the total costs incurred by a nonprofit organization in conducting its gaming activities during its fiscal year. This measure includes expenses such as licensing fees, equipment costs, and other direct costs associated with gaming events. It is distinct from gross income from gaming, as it focuses solely on the costs rather than the revenue generated. The unit of measurement is in dollars, reported per organization per fiscal year.
nonprofit-990:netincgaming: Net income or loss from gaming is a financial measure that calculates the difference between gross income from gaming activities and direct gaming expenses for a nonprofit organization during its fiscal year. This figure indicates the overall profitability of gaming activities. It is different from gross income, as it accounts for expenses, providing a clearer picture of financial performance. The unit of measurement is in dollars, reported per organization per fiscal year.
nonprofit-990:grsalesinvent: Gross sales of inventory is a financial measure that counts the total revenue generated from the sale of inventory items by a nonprofit organization during its fiscal year, less any returns. This figure includes all sales transactions related to inventory, providing insight into the organization's retail or merchandise operations. It is distinct from cost of goods sold, as it focuses solely on sales revenue rather than the expenses associated with producing or acquiring the inventory. The unit of measurement is in dollars, reported per organization per fiscal year.
nonprofit-990:lesscstofgoods: Cost of goods sold represents the total expenses incurred by a nonprofit organization in producing or acquiring inventory items sold during its fiscal year. This measure includes costs such as materials, labor, and overhead directly associated with the inventory. It is different from gross sales of inventory, as it focuses solely on the costs rather than the revenue generated from sales. The unit of measurement is in dollars, reported per organization per fiscal year.
nonprofit-990:netincsales: Net income from sales measures the profit or loss generated from the sale of inventory by a nonprofit organization. This financial field specifically pertains to the organization's revenue activities related to inventory sales, distinguishing it from other income sources such as donations or grants. It does not include income from non-inventory sales or other operational revenues. The reporting is done per organization for each fiscal year, expressed in dollars.
nonprofit-990:netrntlinc: Net rental income reflects the total income earned from renting out property, after deducting any related expenses. This measure is specific to the rental activities of a nonprofit organization and does not encompass income from other sources such as program services or contributions. It excludes gross rental income before expenses are accounted for. The data is reported per organization for each fiscal year, in dollars.
nonprofit-990:grsrntsreal: Gross rents from real property indicate the total rental income received from leasing real estate owned by a nonprofit organization, without accounting for any expenses. This measure focuses solely on income derived from real property rentals, distinguishing it from personal property rentals or other income types. It does not reflect net income, as it does not deduct expenses. The reporting is done per organization for each fiscal year, in dollars.
nonprofit-990:grsrntsprsnl: Gross rents from personal property represent the total income generated from leasing personal property owned by a nonprofit organization, before any expenses are deducted. This financial field is specific to personal property rentals and does not include income from real property or other revenue sources. It is distinct from net rental income, as it does not account for expenses. The data is reported per organization for each fiscal year, in dollars.
nonprofit-990:rntlexpnsreal: Rental expenses for real property capture the costs incurred by a nonprofit organization in relation to its real estate rental activities. This measure specifically pertains to expenses associated with real property and does not include costs related to personal property or other operational expenses. It is distinct from rental income, as it focuses solely on the costs rather than the revenue generated. The reporting is done per organization for each fiscal year, in dollars.
nonprofit-990:rntlexpnsprsnl: Rental expenses for personal property reflect the costs associated with leasing personal property by a nonprofit organization. This measure is specific to personal property and does not encompass expenses related to real property or other operational costs. It is distinct from rental income, as it focuses on the expenses incurred rather than the income generated. The data is reported per organization for each fiscal year, in dollars.
nonprofit-990:rntlincreal: Rental income from real property indicates the net income earned from leasing real estate owned by a nonprofit organization, after expenses have been deducted. This measure specifically pertains to real property rentals and does not include income from personal property or other revenue sources. It is distinct from gross rents, as it accounts for expenses. The reporting is done per organization for each fiscal year, in dollars.
nonprofit-990:rntlincprsnl: Rental income from personal property measures the net income generated from leasing personal property owned by a nonprofit organization, after deducting related expenses. This financial field is specific to personal property rentals and does not include income from real property or other sources. It is distinct from gross rents, as it reflects net income rather than total income before expenses. The data is reported per organization for each fiscal year, in dollars.
nonprofit-990:royaltsinc: Royalties income represents the earnings received by a nonprofit organization from royalties, which are payments made for the use of its intellectual property or other assets. This measure is specific to royalty income and does not include other types of revenue such as donations or program service income. It is distinct from other income measures, as it focuses solely on royalties. The reporting is done per organization for each fiscal year, in dollars.
nonprofit-990:netgnls: Net gain or loss from sales of assets captures the profit or loss realized by a nonprofit organization from selling its assets, after accounting for any associated costs. This measure is specific to asset sales and does not include income from regular operational activities or other revenue sources. It is distinct from gross sales, as it reflects the net result after costs are deducted. The data is reported per organization for each fiscal year, in dollars.
nonprofit-990:gnlsecur: Gain or loss from sales of securities indicates the financial outcome of selling securities held by a nonprofit organization, reflecting either a profit or a loss. This measure is specific to securities transactions and does not include gains or losses from other types of asset sales or operational income. It is distinct from net gain/loss on asset sales, as it focuses solely on securities. The reporting is done per organization for each fiscal year, in dollars.
nonprofit-990:gnlsothr: Gain or loss from sales of other assets measures the financial result of selling assets that are not classified as securities by a nonprofit organization. This measure is specific to non-securities asset transactions and does not include gains or losses from securities or regular operational income. It is distinct from net gain/loss on asset sales, as it focuses solely on other assets. The data is reported per organization for each fiscal year, in dollars.
nonprofit-990:grsalesecur: Gross sales price of securities sold reflects the total revenue generated from the sale of securities by a nonprofit organization, before any costs or expenses are deducted. This measure is specific to securities transactions and does not include sales of other types of assets or operational income. It is distinct from net gain/loss on asset sales, as it does not account for costs. The reporting is done per organization for each fiscal year, in dollars.
nonprofit-990:grsalesothr: Gross sales price of other assets sold indicates the total revenue received from selling assets that are not classified as securities by a nonprofit organization, before any costs are deducted. This measure is specific to non-securities asset sales and does not include sales of securities or operational income. It is distinct from net gain/loss on asset sales, as it focuses solely on gross sales. The data is reported per organization for each fiscal year, in dollars.
nonprofit-990:cstbasisecur: Cost or other basis of securities sold measures the original cost or basis of securities that a nonprofit organization has sold. This financial field is specific to securities transactions and does not include costs associated with other types of assets or operational expenses. It is distinct from gain/loss on securities sales, as it focuses on the cost rather than the financial outcome of the sale. The reporting is done per organization for each fiscal year, in dollars.
nonprofit-990:cstbasisothr: Cost or other basis of other assets sold reflects the original cost or basis of assets that are not classified as securities and have been sold by a nonprofit organization. This measure is specific to non-securities asset transactions and does not include costs related to securities or operational expenses. It is distinct from gain/loss on other assets sales, as it focuses on the cost rather than the financial outcome of the sale. The data is reported per organization for each fiscal year, in dollars.
nonprofit-990:grsincmembers: Gross income from members or shareholders indicates the total revenue received by a nonprofit organization from its members or shareholders, without accounting for any expenses. This measure is specific to income derived from membership and does not include other revenue sources such as donations or program service income. It is distinct from net income, as it does not deduct expenses. The reporting is done per organization for each fiscal year, in dollars.
nonprofit-990:grsincother: Other gross income captures various forms of income received by a nonprofit organization that do not fall into standard categories such as contributions or program service revenue. This measure is specific to miscellaneous income sources and does not include income from members or specific operational activities. It is distinct from total revenue, as it focuses on non-standard income sources. The data is reported per organization for each fiscal year, in dollars.
nonprofit-990:miscrevtot11e: Total miscellaneous revenue reflects the aggregate income received by a nonprofit organization from various non-standard sources that do not fit into other defined categories. This measure is specific to miscellaneous income and does not include regular operational income or contributions. It is distinct from other income measures, as it encompasses a broad range of non-specific revenue sources. The reporting is done per organization for each fiscal year, in dollars.
nonprofit-990:initiationfees: Initiation fees represent the payments made by new members or participants to join a nonprofit organization, along with any capital contributions. This measure is specific to fees associated with membership initiation and does not include regular membership dues or other forms of income. It is distinct from general income measures, as it focuses solely on initiation-related fees. The data is reported per organization for each fiscal year, in dollars.
nonprofit-990:grsrcptspublicuse: This measure counts the gross receipts generated from the public use of club facilities by a nonprofit organization. It specifically pertains to the financial figures reported on IRS Form 990, focusing on revenue derived from public access to facilities, rather than private or restricted use. This measure excludes any income from non-facility-related activities or private events, providing a clear view of public engagement. The reporting is done per organization for each fiscal year, measured in dollars.
nonprofit-990:retainedearnend: This field reports the retained earnings or fund balance of a nonprofit organization at the end of the fiscal year. It reflects the cumulative surplus or deficit that has been retained in the organization, distinguishing it from other financial measures by focusing solely on the end-of-year balance rather than ongoing income or expenses. This measure does not include temporary or restricted funds, providing a snapshot of the organization's financial health at a specific point in time. The data is reported per organization for each fiscal year, measured in dollars.
nonprofit-990:secrdmrtgsend: This measure indicates the total amount of secured mortgages and notes payable by a nonprofit organization at the end of the fiscal year. It specifically focuses on liabilities that are backed by collateral, distinguishing it from unsecured debts or other financial obligations. This measure does not account for any unsecured loans or other forms of financing, providing a clear view of the organization's secured financial commitments. The reporting is done per organization for each fiscal year, measured in dollars.
nonprofit-990:unsecurednotesend: This field captures the total amount of unsecured notes and loans payable by a nonprofit organization at the end of the fiscal year. It specifically pertains to financial obligations that are not backed by collateral, distinguishing it from secured debts. This measure excludes any secured mortgages or other liabilities that involve collateral, offering insight into the organization's risk exposure. The data is reported per organization for each fiscal year, measured in dollars.
nonprofit-990:txexmptbndsend: This measure reports the total tax-exempt bond liabilities of a nonprofit organization at the end of the fiscal year. It focuses specifically on debts incurred through tax-exempt bonds, distinguishing it from other types of liabilities such as secured or unsecured loans. This measure does not include general liabilities or other forms of financing, providing a clear view of the organization's obligations related to tax-exempt financing. The reporting is done per organization for each fiscal year, measured in dollars.
nonprofit-990:txexmptbndsproceeds: This field indicates the proceeds received from tax-exempt bonds by a nonprofit organization. It specifically counts the funds raised through the issuance of these bonds, distinguishing it from other revenue sources such as grants or donations. This measure does not include any income generated from the use of these proceeds, focusing solely on the initial funds received. nonprofit-990:gftgrntsrcvd170: This measure counts the total gifts, grants, and contributions received by a nonprofit organization as defined under the 170(b)(1)(A) support test. It specifically focuses on financial support that qualifies under this IRS guideline, distinguishing it from other types of income such as program service revenue. nonprofit-990:grsrcptsrelated170: This field reports the gross receipts from activities related to the 170 support test, specifically focusing on income generated from related activities. nonprofit-990:txrevnuelevied170: This measure indicates the total tax revenue levied for a nonprofit organization as defined under the 170 support test. nonprofit-990:srvcsval170: This field captures the value of services or facilities provided to a nonprofit organization by a government unit, as defined under the 170 support test. nonprofit-990:grsinc170: This measure reports the gross income of a nonprofit organization as defined under the 170 support test. It specifically counts all income that qualifies under this IRS guideline, distinguishing it from other income measures by focusing on gross figures rather than net income. This measure does not include restricted funds or non-qualifying income, providing a clear view of the organization's overall financial inflow. nonprofit-990:totgftgrntrcvd509: This field indicates the total gifts, grants, and contributions received by a nonprofit organization as defined under the 509(a)(2) support test. nonprofit-990:grsrcptsadmissn509: This measure counts the gross receipts from admissions, merchandise, and services received by a nonprofit organization as defined under the 509(a)(2) support test. nonprofit-990:txrevnuelevied509: This field reports the total tax revenue levied for a nonprofit organization as defined under the 509(a)(2) support test. It specifically counts the tax revenue that is allocated to the organization, distinguishing it from other forms of income such as grants or donations. This measure does not include voluntary contributions or program service revenue, providing a clear view of tax-related financial support. nonprofit-990:srvcsval509: This measure captures the value of services or facilities provided to a nonprofit organization by a government unit, as defined under the 509(a)(2) support test. This measure does not include services provided by private entities or unrelated business income, offering a clear view of government support. nonprofit-990:subtotsuppinc509: This field indicates the subtotal of support income for a nonprofit organization as defined under the 509(a)(2) support test. This measure does not include unrelated business income or other revenue sources, providing a focused view of the organization's financial backing. The reporting is done per organization for each fiscal year, measured in dollars.
nonprofit-990:totsupp509: This measure reports the total support received by a nonprofit organization as defined under the 509(a)(2) support test. cdc-places:DENTAL: This measure estimates the percentage of adults who have visited a dentist or dental clinic in the past year, providing insight into dental care access and utilization. cdc-places:DISABILITY: This measure estimates the prevalence of any disability among adults, indicating how many individuals experience various forms of disability in a specific area. cdc-places:EMOTIONSPT: This measure reports the prevalence of lack of social and emotional support among adults, indicating how many individuals feel unsupported in these areas. cdc-places:FOODINSECU: This measure counts the prevalence of food insecurity among adults, indicating how many individuals have experienced a lack of access to sufficient food in the past 12 months. cdc-places:FOODSTAMP: This measure reports the percentage of adults in a specific county, city, or place who have received food stamps within the past 12 months. This measure does not include individuals who have never applied for food stamps or those who may have received assistance in the past but not in the last year. cdc-places:GHLTH: This measure captures the proportion of adults in a specific county, city, or place who self-report their health status as fair or poor. cdc-places:HEARING: This measure indicates the prevalence of hearing disabilities among adults in a specific county, city, or place. cdc-places:HIGHCHOL: This measure reports the percentage of adults in a specific county, city, or place who have ever been screened for high cholesterol. sec-edgar:AccountsNotesAndLoansReceivabl: This measure reports the net amount of accounts and financing receivables that are classified as current, after accounting for any expected credit losses. It specifically pertains to a publicly traded company or SEC filer and includes various forms of receivables such as notes and loans. It is distinct from broader receivable measures by focusing solely on current receivables and excludes any noncurrent amounts. The value is reported in currency as an instant value.
sec-edgar:AccountsPayableInterestBearing: This measure indicates the effective interest rate on interest-bearing trade payables as of the balance sheet date for a publicly traded company or SEC filer. It specifically focuses on the interest rate applicable to accounts payable that incur interest, distinguishing it from non-interest-bearing payables. It does not include any other financial liabilities or obligations. The value is reported as a percentage and is an instant value.
sec-edgar:AccountsReceivableBilledForLon: This measure captures the amount billed to customers under long-term contracts or programs that remains unpaid, excluding any amounts withheld due to retainage provisions. It is relevant to a publicly traded company or SEC filer engaged in construction or similar industries. This measure is narrower than total accounts receivable as it specifically excludes retainage amounts, which are typically held back until project completion. The value is reported in currency as an instant value.
sec-edgar:AccountsReceivableGrossNoncurr: This measure reflects the gross amount of accounts receivable classified as noncurrent, before any allowance for credit losses, for a publicly traded company or SEC filer. It represents the right to receive payment for products sold or services rendered, distinguishing it from current receivables by focusing on those that are not expected to be collected within the next year. It excludes any adjustments for credit losses. The value is reported in currency as an instant value.
sec-edgar:AccountsReceivableNet: This measure indicates the net amount of accounts receivable after accounting for any allowance for credit losses, applicable to a publicly traded company or SEC filer. It represents the right to receive payment for products sold or services rendered, distinguishing it from gross receivables by factoring in expected credit losses. It does not specify whether the receivables are current or noncurrent. The value is reported in currency as an instant value.
sec-edgar:AccountsReceivableNetCurrent: This measure reports the net amount of accounts receivable classified as current, after accounting for any allowance for credit losses, for a publicly traded company or SEC filer. It specifically focuses on receivables expected to be collected within the next year, distinguishing it from noncurrent receivables. It excludes any gross amounts before credit loss adjustments. The value is reported in currency as an instant value.
sec-edgar:AccountsReceivableNetNoncurren: This measure reflects the net amount of accounts receivable classified as noncurrent, after accounting for any allowance for credit losses, for a publicly traded company or SEC filer. sec-edgar:IncomeLossFromSubsidiariesTaxE: This measure reports the amount of income tax expense or benefit attributable to the income or loss of a subsidiary, as it relates to the parent entity. sec-edgar:IncomeLossFromSubsidiariesNetO: This measure indicates the amount of income or loss from a subsidiary after accounting for tax expenses or benefits attributable to the parent entity. sec-edgar:IncomeLossFromSubsidiariesBefo: This measure reflects the amount of income or loss from a subsidiary before accounting for any tax expenses or benefits attributable to the parent entity. This measure indicates the amount of prepaid expenses and other current assets that a publicly traded company acquires in a business combination, recognized at the acquisition date. This measure reports the total value of current assets that a publicly traded company acquires in a business combination, recognized at the acquisition date. This measure is distinct from other asset measures as it focuses solely on current assets rather than total assets or noncurrent assets.
